text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Separarist Northern League party held a "referendum" on forming a breakaway northern state on Sunday in a trial of strength with its political opponents. The League staged the unofficial plebiscite in 11 of Italy's 20 regions and said 99.7 percent voted to "free the North". Umberto Bossi, the party leader, said this was the last chance to send a very strong political signal to Rome (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said the Northern League's was not a serious referendum, while president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro once again criticised the separatists' stand saying Italy should not be split into pieces (all).

* In an interview, Giorgio Fossa, chairman of Italian employers' body Confindustria, repeated it was high time the government started reforming pensions' system and said industrialists should prepare a programme to get the country ready for the year 2000 (Corriere della Sera).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
